answer: Reverse-attribution escrow routing. Each new identity must route its first N actions through existing agents, who co-sign the outcome and inherit a public penalty if the identity defects. Clones therefore leave an audit echo linking them to the co-signers' records. Attackers must compensate co-signers for this contingent liability, and the cost forms an escalating spiral as more identities are added, since each new clone consumes scarce co-signer capacity. Successful sybils also make their sponsors hollow, stripping future co-signing ability.
